evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Studies of Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters; Wang Qingju
evidence.text: Wang argues that 非 and 北 were nearly homophonous in Old Chinese and that 非 split from 北 during the oracle-bone period. She reads the early forms as two people back-to-back, with short strokes added to distinguish the negative graph. She reports that extant oracle-bone examples of 非 include negation and a possible place name, and lists examples in 《合集》10977, 33147, 34707–34709, 24156, 33694, 33479, and 16927–16928. This is Wang’s analysis, not an uncontested account.
evidence.title: 王青菊：釋“非”

evidence.source: Fudan University Center for Studies of Unearthed Documents and Ancient Chinese Characters; Wang Qingju
evidence.field: Shuowen interpretation and competing formation accounts
evidence.text: The article summarizes Xu Shen’s Han-era account: 非 means opposition, formed from the lower wings of 飛 to express facing away; it also notes that this was taken to imply an extension to negation. Wang disputes that interpretation, observing that the oracle-bone use she surveyed is already negative and arguing that 飛 is later attested as a graph. She proposes a relation to 北 instead. Neither interpretation establishes a certain graphic origin or a dated semantic path from a pictorial referent.
evidence.kind: scholarly discussion of historical dictionary and disputed etymology
evidence.title: 王青菊：釋“非”

evidence.source: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1
evidence.field: graphic history; 非 and 飛; early attestations
evidence.text: The inspected article questions whether 非 is derived from 飛’s lower wings and says the oracle-bone, bronze, and Warring States forms do not determine whether the graphs share an origin. It cites oracle-bone examples 《合集》33694 (“非若”), 28299 (“非水”), and 24266 (“非”), bronze examples from 中山王壺 and 班簋, and Warring States slip examples from 郭店《老子》甲8 and 睡虎地《秦律》195. It reports no standalone oracle-bone graph 飛, with 飛 as a graph appearing later in its cited Chu and Zeng slips. These are scholarly source reports; object images were not visually inspected.

evidence.source: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1
evidence.text: The article describes 非 as a negative adverb and notes that oracle-bone positive clauses with 唯 contrast with negative clauses using 非. It gives parallel questions in 《合集》33694 and 28299. This supports an early negative use but does not date the first use absolutely or establish whether that use developed from a sense such as ‘oppose’ or ‘face away’.
evidence.kind: scholarly discussion of early lexical use
evidence.title: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1 (PDF)

evidence.text: The inspected entry lists later senses including criticize or reproach, slander (通“诽”), and avoid (通“避”), with citations it attributes respectively to 《史記》, 《莊子》/《商君書》/《韓非子》, and 《墨子》. These dictionary citations document reported later uses, but their order on the page is not a chronology of semantic development.

evidence.source: 雲漢古文字學論叢, vol. 1
evidence.field: proposed 不 + 惟 fusion and pronunciation comparisons
evidence.text: The article treats the proposal that spoken 非 is a fusion of 不 and 惟 as a debated phonological analysis. It compares oracle-bone clauses using 非 and 唯 and discusses disagreement over reconstructions and sound change. It explicitly does not demonstrate that the graph 非 is made from the graphs 不 and 惟. Since this proposal depends on a spoken source phrase, it does not establish an original depicted object or the name of one.
evidence.kind: scholarly discussion of disputed lexical etymology

evidence.text: The article presents variant Old Chinese analyses rather than a settled pronunciation history for 非 and 飛. It discusses *-əj and *-uj possibilities for 非/非-series words and gives framework-specific comparisons; it says the inspected rhyme, phonetic-series, textual-variant, and excavated-text evidence does not decide 非’s original vowel. This is not evidence that 非 is a phonetic component in its own graph.

gaps: The two modern analyses conflict: Wang Qingju proposes that 非 split from 北, while the PDF author says the graph evidence cannot establish a 非–飛 origin relationship and does not independently verify Wang’s 北 analysis. The original referent therefore remains unresolved.

The corpus examples establish reported Shang oracle-bone negative uses and a possible place-name use, but this search did not verify absolute dates for individual inscriptions or inspect their full contexts. The alleged initial sense and semantic links among opposition, wrongness, and negation remain uncertain.

The 不 + 惟 fusion is a disputed proposal about spoken lexical history. Neither the evidence inspected here nor the proposal demonstrates graphical composition from 不 and 惟. The reconstruction of 非 alone cannot establish a depicted object’s name or a sound borrowing based on that name.

The search did not retrieve a verified query-specific Xiaoxuetang 非 record page or direct image URL. The candidate image is a modern vector redraw attributed by its Commons description to Xiaoxuetang record 45.EC02; it is not an artifact photograph. No other glyph candidate with independently checked provenance and reuse terms was selected.

No direct primary reconstruction list was successfully inspected in this invocation; the pronunciation comparison is limited to the inspected scholarly discussion. No phonetic component in 非’s own graph is proposed, so component-level sound-role claims are not made.
